title: Armed gang robs gold shop in Narathiwat mall
detail: Khaosod English reported an armed gang robbed a gold shop inside a shopping mall in Narathiwat and one officer was injured; the army linked the heist to insurgent funding and the defence minister said BRN carried it out (per Thai Examiner, 7 Oct).
attribution: outlet reporting; Royal Thai Army and Defence Ministry (insurgency link)
note: headline only; The Pattaya News reported two people injured and about 24 million baht in valuables taken; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Police officer and militant killed in Pattani gunfight
detail: Thai Newsroom reported a policeman was killed in a clash with insurgents in Pattani; The Nation reported the gunfight took place at an Islamic school and one militant was shot dead.
note: headlines only (Thai Newsroom; The Nation 40056849); Thai PBS World describes the dead officer as a security officer; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Bomb at tea shop in Narathiwat kills two
detail: A bomb went off at a tea shop in Narathiwat on Thursday 16 October; Thai Examiner reported on 22 Oct that the death toll had risen to two, including an elderly woman. The Nation reported three police and six civilians injured, while The Star reported 14 injured.
note: headlines only; injury figures differ between outlets (9 per The Nation, 14 per The Star); Bernama reported a blast injuring 10 in Yi-ngo district that may be the same event; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Thailand and BRN agree to resume peace dialogue
detail: Malay Mail reported the Thai government and the Patani Malay BRN would resume the southern peace dialogue with Malaysia as facilitator and host; The Nation separately reported a new head of the Thai peace panel held a special meeting with BRN.
attribution: Thai government and BRN (via Malaysian facilitator)
note: headline only

title: SBPAC releases 22-year Deep South toll
detail: SBPAC figures based on certified compensation cases counted 10,116 incidents, 5,999 deaths and 13,519 injured from January 2004 to December 2025; 2025 alone had 150 certified incidents and 48 deaths.

title: Thai government and BRN meet in Malaysia
detail: Prachatai reported the Thai panel led by NIA head Thanat Suwannanon met BRN representatives in Malaysia on 8-9 January 2026 and that the meeting ended badly over BRN demands for self-governance.

title: Coordinated bombings hit 11 PTT petrol stations
detail: Bombs and fires struck 11 PTT petrol stations within about 40 minutes: five in Narathiwat, two in Pattani and four in Yala. The army and officials reported four injured (a police officer, a firefighter and two station staff); the military imposed a curfew in Narathiwat.
place: Multiple sites incl. Ban Khok, Chuap (Cho-airong); Dusongyo (Chanae); Ra-ngae; Waeng; Su-ngai Kolok; Mueang Pattani; Kapho; Kabang; Bannang Sata; Mueang Yala
attribution: Thai Army; Narathiwat governor (injury count via The Defense Post)

title: Night curfew imposed in Narathiwat after petrol-station attacks
detail: Malay Mail reported Thailand imposed an immediate curfew in Narathiwat after a spate of explosions at petrol stations; The Nation reported a 9 pm to 5 am curfew, and The Star reported on 12 Jan that the government had lifted it.
note: security response to the 11 Jan petrol-station attacks already recorded; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Gunfight as troops move to arrest Yala petrol-station attack suspects
detail: Thai Newsroom reported a gunfight erupted when troops cordoned a hideout in Yala to arrest suspects in the petrol-station arson attacks; The Nation reported an alleged insurgent suspect linked to those attacks was shot dead.
note: headlines only (also The Star 2026-01-20, The Nation 40061476); province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Bomb explodes during assembly in Yala house
detail: A device went off inside a house in Moo 1, Ban Yala while it was being assembled, seriously injuring the bomb-maker. ISOC Region 4 Forward Command said parts were linked to an insurgent group.
attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

title: Toilet time-bomb wounds EOD officer at Pattani petrol station
detail: Timed devices were found in toilets at three PTT stations in Mueang Pattani; the third, at Talubo, exploded during disposal on 4 February and injured a bomb-disposal police officer. Thairath reported the devices were timed for 14 February.
place: PTT station, Talubo subdistrict (also Sabarang and Ruesamilae sites)

title: Suspected bomb found in Pattani bus terminal restroom
detail: A suspected homemade bomb was found in the women's restroom of the Pattani bus terminal and the terminal was evacuated. The Star called it the third such find in three days, after devices at petrol stations.
note: also The Star, 5 Feb (https://www.thestar.com.my/aseanplus/aseanplus-news/2026/02/05/suspected-bomb-found-at-bus-terminal-in-thai-province-of-pattani-incident-is-third-in-three-days); coordinates are the town centre

title: IED hits army convoy near Ban Wang Hin bridge, Bannang Sata
detail: An IED was detonated against a REVA armoured vehicle of a rapid-response infantry unit securing election routes, injuring one soldier; Thairath said an exchange of gunfire followed.
place: Ban Wang Hin bridge, Ban Tue-ra

title: Culvert gas-cylinder bomb misses police, hurts three villagers
detail: A roughly 50 kg gas-cylinder bomb planted in a road culvert exploded as a police vehicle passed but hit a civilian pickup behind it, injuring three villagers. Authorities blamed insurgents trying to ambush police.

title: Seven overnight bombs hit shops in Yi-ngo and Ra-ngae
detail: Seven small bombs exploded between 23:00 on 14 February and 05:00 on 15 February at shops and a house in Yi-ngo and at two sites in Tanyong Mas (Ra-ngae). No injuries were reported.
place: Five sites in Yi-ngo; two in Tanyong Mas

title: ISOC Region 4 detains 11 over PTT petrol-station arson
detail: ISOC Region 4 said it had detained 11 suspects over the January arson and bomb attacks on PTT stations; officials said members of a Narathiwat cell had learned bomb-making online.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Roadside bomb misses prisoner-escort vehicle on Ban Niang–Yaha road
detail: A roadside bomb went off on the Ban Niang–Yaha road, apparently aimed at a vehicle carrying a suspect in custody. It missed its target.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Roadside bomb injures two in Bannang Sata
detail: Khaosod English reported a roadside bomb injured two people in Yala's Bannang Sata district after spray-painted messages were found in the area.
note: headline only; victim category not stated in headline

title: Suspect killed in Nong Chik siege
detail: Security forces surrounded a house holding a security-case suspect, who fired at a drone and officers and threw an explosive; officials said the suspected insurgent was killed.

title: Border patrol policeman and suspect killed in Nong Chik clash
detail: A 10-minute firefight in a rubber plantation after security forces surrounded suspects killed a Border Patrol Police officer and one suspected insurgent. The Pattani Task Force commander linked suspects to the 'Wae Aree' network.
place: Moo 6, Ban Pakalue Song, Tuiyong subdistrict

title: Bomb at Thanam outpost injures five officers
detail: An IED left on a motorcycle sidecar exploded outside the Thanam strategic outpost, starting a fire and injuring five officers' hearing. Police said it was likely retaliation for the Nong Chik clashes.
place: Thanam outpost, Ban Kha, Thanam subdistrict

title: Gunmen fire on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak's vehicle
detail: Gunmen in a pickup fired more than 10 rounds at the car of Prachachat MP Kamolsak Leewamoh outside his Bacho home; he was unharmed but his driver and police bodyguard were wounded. Police later identified former military personnel as suspects and HRW reported an ISOC-registered vehicle was used, so this is not an insurgent attack.

title: Bomb and fire destroy Mini Big C in Thung Yang Daeng
detail: An explosion and fire destroyed a Mini Big C convenience store in Thung Yang Daeng district early in the morning, after it had closed. No casualties were reported.
note: date from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review (the source URL carries no date); Khaosod English also posted it; casualties not stated in the headline; coordinates are the district centre

title: Father and son arrested over attack on Narathiwat MP's car
detail: Police arrested a father and son, both former marines, over the March gun attack on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak's vehicle. Two more suspects were being sought.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Deputy district chief and companion killed in Chanae ambush
detail: About eight gunmen fired on a parked pickup at Ban Sue, killing deputy district chief Monchai Jitkamolkarn and a 27-year-old; an M16 was taken. Police said personal motives were also being examined.

title: Village headman shot dead in Sai Buri
detail: Headman Reeya Salae was shot while riding to dawn prayers and died in hospital; police were considering a personal dispute as well as insurgency.

title: 500 local leaders rally against violence after Chanae killings
detail: About 500 sub-district and village heads gathered to reject violence and condemn the killing of a senior deputy district chief and a local-administration official.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Four rangers badly wounded in Chanae ambush
detail: Gunmen ambushed a ranger unit in Chanae district, seriously wounding four rangers. A company commander led the pursuit.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Region 9 police report 27 arrests in Deep South sweep
detail: The Provincial Police Region 9 commander said a sweep had led to 27 arrests. In the case of the attack on the Narathiwat MP, three people had been arrested and two were still being sought.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Suspected bomb found by road and teacher's residence burns in Pattani
detail: Thai Newsroom reported a bomb-like object was found beside a road and a teacher's residence caught fire in Pattani.
note: headline only; cause of fire not stated; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Pattani court jails bombers over Sai Buri attack
detail: Pattani Provincial Court sentenced a group of defendants to 10 years and 6 months in prison for a bombing in Sai Buri district.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Intelligence chief named head of southern peace dialogue team
detail: Thai Enquirer reported the National Security Council appointed Tanat Suwannanon, director of the National Intelligence Agency, as the new head of the southern peace dialogue team and expanded cooperation with Malaysia; Thai PBS World and the Bangkok Post also reported the appointment.
note: date derived from the post's timestamp

title: Roadside bomb wounds one officer in Pattani
detail: A roadside bomb wounded one officer in Pattani. The supplied review places it on Route 42 in Yaring district and says it damaged a Royal Thai Navy task-force vehicle.
note: headline only; date, district, road and unit from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; coordinates are the district centre

title: Suspect arrested over bombing of rangers in Yala
detail: Police arrested a suspect in a bomb attack on rangers in Yala. They said the operation followed the law and respected human rights.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Navy captain answers summons in MP shooting probe
detail: A navy captain linked to the case of the attack on Narathiwat MP Kamolsak reported to investigators at Narathiwat provincial police. Separately, Justice Minister Tawee said key evidence in the case was still incomplete.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Roadside bomb hits ranger convoy on Highway 4057
detail: A roadside bomb struck Ranger Task Force 11 personnel near Nam Khao bridge. The Nation reported one ranger killed and two injured; an earlier Khaosod report said three were injured.
place: Road 4057 near Ban Mai Fad, Kayu Khla subdistrict

title: Defence volunteer badly wounded by gunmen in Chanae
detail: Gunmen pulled up beside a defence volunteer (Or Sor) as he rode home to his quarters in Chanae and shot him. He was seriously wounded.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Police sergeant killed in attack on new Sai Buri police station
detail: Gunmen fired on officers at a base beside the unfinished Sai Buri police station; a police sergeant major, 29, died. Officials said it bore hallmarks of insurgent violence. Thai Examiner described it as a 'Friday evening' attack, which matches 22 May; its dateline is 23 May.
place: Sai Buri police station compound, Tabing subdistrict

title: Hijab-clad gunmen kill teacher outside Yarang school
detail: Four attackers dressed as women fired on a police officer's car outside a school, killing his wife, a teacher who was holding their infant, and wounding the officer. ISOC Region 4 condemned the attack as inhumane.
place: Near Prasan Wittaya Foundation School, Pong Sta subdistrict
attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

title: Life sentence for Panare bombing
detail: A court sentenced a defendant in a Panare district bombing case to life in prison. It also ordered more than 3.6 million baht in compensation.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Suspect in Pattani petrol-station bombings arrested in Bangkok
detail: A 21-year-old was arrested at Bangkok's central railway station; authorities alleged he acted as a lookout in the February Pattani petrol-station bombings.
place: Bangkok Central Railway Station (case: Mueang Pattani)

title: Ranger killed in Chanae raid on suspects
detail: Suspects linked to the 1 April Chanae ambush fired on security forces during a dawn raid and escaped into forest; one ranger was killed.

title: Two suspected insurgents killed in pre-dawn Pattani firefight
detail: Thai Examiner reported two insurgents died in a pre-dawn firefight with security forces in Pattani after refusing calls to surrender; Malay Mail reported the two men were suspected members of a separatist movement.
note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Bomb outside school in Yala injures two police and a civilian
detail: The Star reported a bombing outside a school in Yala province injured two police officers and one civilian.
note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Arson attack on Pattani solar farm construction site
detail: Khaosod English reported assailants broke into a solar power plant construction site in Pattani early on Monday 15 June and set fire to a solar panel storage area, causing damage but no casualties; authorities launched a manhunt.
note: The Nation (40067197) reported an armed attack and blast at a Pattani power plant that closed a highway, probably the same incident; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Man, 67, shot three times in Cho-airong ambush
detail: Gunmen ambushed a 67-year-old man in Cho-airong district and hit him with three shots. Though seriously wounded, he drove off to get help.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Two separate bombings injure police in Yala and Pattani
detail: The Star reported two separate bombings injured police officers in Yala and Pattani provinces.
note: headline only; two incidents in two provinces, so no coordinates; injury count not in headline; the Yala blast is also recorded on its own at Than To (Bangkok Post), and Bangkok Post reported five police injured in the Pattani blast

title: Roadside bomb injures six border patrol police in Than To
detail: A bomb hit a Border Patrol Police unit on teacher-protection duty in Yala, injuring six officers, two of them seriously.
note: headline only; district and teacher-protection duty from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; also VietnamPlus; one of the two blasts in The Star's 19 Jun record; coordinates are the district centre

title: Bomb under police pickup explodes after child raises alarm
detail: A child saw a man at a police vehicle outside Darussadah Mosque; the device attached to the chassis exploded about ten minutes later while waiting for bomb disposal teams. No one was hurt. Investigators blamed insurgent affiliates.
place: Outside Darussadah Mosque, Ban Buketa, Lochut subdistrict

title: Truck torched on Yala-Betong highway
detail: A ten-wheel truck was set on fire near a bridge at Ban Khlong Nam Khun, blocking Highway 410.

title: Bomb outside Thung Yang Daeng religious school injures four
detail: A bomb exploded outside a religious school (pondok) in Thung Yang Daeng, injuring four people, including two children.
note: date and district from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review (the source URL carries no date); also Chiang Rai Times; coordinates are the district centre

title: Defence volunteer shot dead after school run in Yarang
detail: Volunteer Defence Corps member Abdulloh Yama was killed while returning from taking his child to a tadika school; the motive was under investigation.
place: Ban Ton Makham, Mo Mawi subdistrict

title: Tak Bai car-bomb defendant jailed after confession
detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court sentenced a defendant in a Tak Bai car-bomb case to 5 years and 12 months after the defendant confessed.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Three PT petrol stations bombed in Yala and Pattani
detail: About six men in black planted devices that caused explosions and fires at PT stations in Mueang Yala, Sai Buri and Yaring; one person was injured at the Sai Buri station. Authorities suspected insurgents.
place: Sateng Nok (Mueang Yala); Pawa (Sai Buri); Piya (Yaring)

title: Culvert bomb in Tak Bai injures two Malaysian tourists
detail: Khaosod English and The Star reported a bomb blast in Narathiwat's Tak Bai district injured two Malaysian tourists; The Nation described it as a road-culvert blast, and Malaysian police said the pair had entered Thailand legally.
note: headline only; part of the same weekend as the PT petrol-station attacks already recorded on 2026-06-28, but a separate incident

title: 28 BRN-linked suspects detained in two-month operation
detail: The Star reported Thai authorities detained 28 suspects linked to the separatist group BRN during a two-month security operation.
note: headline only; figure covers a two-month period across the region

title: BRN blames slow peace talks for surge in violence
detail: Mizzima reported BRN claimed that slow progress in peace talks was behind a surge of violence in southern Thailand; the New Straits Times reported BRN saying the peace process remained key to resolving the conflict.
note: headline only

title: Sawmill owner shot dead in Bannang Sata ambush
detail: Gunmen ambushed and killed a sawmill owner in Bannang Sata. The mill had been shot at and set on fire several times before.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Malaysia pledges to work with new Thai peace dialogue chief
detail: The Star reported Malaysia would cooperate closely with the new Thai peace dialogue chief, Thanut Suvarnananda; Bernama quoted Malaysian minister Mohamed Khaled.
note: headline only

title: Car bomb explodes outside old Tanyong police station
detail: A 70 kg car bomb driven toward the old Tanyong police station exploded, lightly injuring a police officer. The Nation said it was the 68th car bombing linked to the insurgency since 2005; Al Jazeera said it was the first of 2026.
place: Old Tanyong police station, Kaluwo Nuea subdistrict

title: Five rangers killed in Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack
detail: Six to 10 attackers fired at the checkpoint and threw pipe bombs, killing five rangers, wounding five to six civilians and taking rifles. The government called it terrorism.
place: Bukeh Sami checkpoint, Tanyong Mas municipality
attribution: Internal Security Operations Command; Al Jazeera citing ISOC Region 4 reports 6 injured

title: Construction foreman shot dead at Bannang Sata road site
detail: Two hooded men on a motorcycle shot dead a construction foreman supervising road repairs. Police said it was part of insurgent efforts to stir unrest.

title: Martial law enforced across Narathiwat after checkpoint attack
detail: Thai Newsroom and The Star reported martial law was declared in Narathiwat to track down suspects after the 22 July attack that killed five rangers at a checkpoint; The Pattaya News said the Narathiwat task force extended martial-law powers.
note: response to the checkpoint attack already recorded on 2026-07-22; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Warrants issued for checkpoint and car-bomb suspects
detail: ISOC Region 4 Forward Command said warrants were issued for three suspects: one for the Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack and two for the Tanyong car bomb.
attribution: Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 Forward Command

title: Off-duty police sergeant wounded by four gunmen
detail: Four gunmen shot an off-duty police sergeant in the thigh; he returned fire and the attackers escaped by motorcycle and boat.

title: Guns from Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack linked to Chanae killing
detail: Police said forensic tests showed that some guns used in the 22 July Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack were linked to the earlier shooting of a Chanae deputy district chief.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Thailand suspends peace talks with BRN; September meeting cancelled
detail: The Star reported Thailand suspended peace talks with the southern insurgent group and called off a meeting planned in Malaysia for September; Bernama said the Narathiwat attack forced the talks on hold, and Malay Mail (31 Jul) said the attacks prompted Thailand to rethink the dialogue.
note: headline only

title: Narathiwat residents march for peace as talks stall
detail: Thai Examiner reported people in Narathiwat marched to demand peace after the 22 July attack derailed the Malaysia-facilitated talks.
note: headline only; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Two police killed in Tak Bai shootout during drug operation
detail: A suspect opened fire on Tak Bai police during an anti-drug operation near a palm plantation, killing two officers and injuring four. Authorities later linked the group to the Bukeh Sami checkpoint attack.

title: Bomb in official vehicle explodes in Dusongyo
detail: An IED in an official vehicle exploded at about 18:45, damaging it; authorities said no one was injured.

title: Hearing in MP Kamolsak shooting case postponed to 18 Sep
detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court postponed the witness examination of six defendants in the case of the shooting at MP Kamolsak's vehicle to 18 September 2026.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Two suspects in Tak Bai police killings shot dead in Sukhirin
detail: Police said the two suspects fired first when cornered in a house and were killed. Eleven people were detained for sheltering them, and the network was linked to the Bukeh Sami attack.

title: Yarang raid finds guns, contraband cigarettes and 18m baht
detail: ISOC Region 4 searched a suspect house in Yarang district and found illegal cigarettes, firearms and more than 18 million baht in cash.
note: headline/snippet only

title: 51 coordinated attacks across three provinces in one night
detail: Between about 20:00 and midnight, attackers carried out arson, bombings and shootings against local government offices, telecom towers, CCTV, power poles and shops; the army said 51 incidents occurred. The Nation counted 34 (14 Yala, 13 Narathiwat, 5 Pattani), and Thai Examiner later cited 78 including two in Songkhla.
attribution: Thai military; Lt Gen Norathip Poinok (via The Nation)

title: Roadside bomb wounds three civilians in Narathiwat
detail: Al Jazeera reported that a roadside bomb in Narathiwat during the night's coordinated attacks wounded two women and a man. The exact site was not given.

title: Gunmen torch government vehicles at Ban Rae SAO, Than To
detail: During the coordinated attacks, government vehicles were set on fire at the Ban Rae subdistrict administrative office and a telecom tower was set alight at Si Tha Nam.

title: Armed men bomb and burn Bang Pu convenience store
detail: At about 20:45 at least five armed men cleared a roadside convenience store, fired into the air and left an IED that exploded about 30 minutes later, destroying the building. No casualties were reported.
place: Moo 3, Ban Bang Pu, Bang Pu subdistrict

title: Explosive damages railway sleepers at Maruebo, Ra-ngae
detail: The State Railway of Thailand found concrete sleepers damaged after the overnight attacks and closed the Narathiwat section. Three more blasts followed on Sunday morning in Pattani and Narathiwat, with no injuries.

title: At least 15 attackers raid Phoming municipal office
detail: At least 15 attackers subdued guards, burned four municipal vehicles and part of the office, and set off an IED near the guard booth. No casualties were reported. Khaosod dated its report 23 August; the raid may belong to the 22 August wave.

title: SBPAC/Isranews: 103 incidents in 2026 through July
detail: Figures verified with SBPAC and Isranews's southern news centre put incidents at 1,271 from 2017 to 31 July 2026, including 103 incidents and 245 casualties in 2026.
attribution: SBPAC; Isranews Agency Southern News Centre

title: Narathiwat imposes curfew after wave of bomb and arson attacks
detail: The Star and the New Straits Times reported Narathiwat imposed a curfew after multiple bomb and arson attacks across the southern border provinces.
note: security response to the 22-24 Aug attacks already recorded; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital

title: Suspect detained in Cho-airong after 40-site Narathiwat attacks
detail: Police detained a man whom CCTV allegedly showed smashing a security camera in Ban Ku Rong; he denied involvement.

title: Gunmen bomb 7-Eleven in Mayo
detail: Armed men ordered people out of a 7-Eleven, set fuel and an IED that burned the store, and exchanged fire with police as they fled. Officials suspected the BRN.
note: Thai Examiner (25 Aug) dates the attack to Monday, 24 Aug

title: Southern army chief: two months' warning did not stop the 51 attacks
detail: Fourth Army commander Lt Gen Norathip Poinok said the army had general warning for nearly two months that government offices, high-voltage lines, convenience stores and large shops could be attacked, but no precise targets.
note: an official's account of prior threat reporting; general warning, not tactical foreknowledge

title: Chanae teen badly wounded; family blames army helicopter
detail: A teenager in Chanae was seriously wounded. His brother says the shots came from an army helicopter after the teen raised his hands. The army says it flew the helicopter but used no weapons, and a House military committee has raised the case.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Masked gunmen storm Global House store and set off bombs
detail: Five masked gunmen cleared the Global House store, planted three devices and left a 50 kg gas-cylinder bomb on a motorcycle sidecar; the explosions caused no casualties.

title: Motorcycle bomb hits police pickup on Route 42, Pattani
detail: A bomb on a motorcycle went off as a police pickup passed; Thaiger reported the officers were unharmed. Outlets differ on whether the site is in Mayo or Panare district.
note: headline only; date and road from the supplied 28 Sep 2026 IED review; district reported inconsistently (Mayo or Panare), so placed between the two

title: Bomb and arson attack on Taluban municipal office
detail: Attackers bombed and set fire to the Taluban town municipality office in Sai Buri; the Fourth Army commander said they meant to bring the building down. House Speaker Wan Noor visited on 13 Sep; the attack came earlier and its exact date is not in the headlines.
attribution: Fourth Army Region commander (per Nation TV headline)
note: headline/snippet only

title: Two jailed six months over arson of six PTT stations
detail: Narathiwat Provincial Court sentenced two defendants to six months in prison over arson attacks on six PTT petrol stations.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Bomb and gun ambush on defence volunteer truck in Sukhirin
detail: Insurgents detonated a roadside gas-cylinder bomb under a truck carrying defence volunteers to a boat race and then opened fire, killing two and wounding 16.
place: Highway 4115, Ban Barukaya-ing, Rom Sai subdistrict

title: Separatists vow to keep fighting as peace talks stall
detail: Al Jazeera reported Malay-Muslim separatists in southern Thailand vowed to keep fighting as peace talks stalled; Malay Mail reported the insurgent group was seeking power, not only talks, with Malaysia at the table.
note: headline only

title: Assistant village headman shot dead in Bannang Sata
detail: Gunmen shot an assistant village headman, 42, with a shotgun as he rode his motorcycle. Investigators had not ruled out a personal dispute.
place: Ban Kuelong, Moo 2, Taling Chan subdistrict

title: Construction vehicles torched and CCTV destroyed on Highway 410
detail: Around 02:30 attackers burned tyres, scattered road spikes, destroyed two CCTV cameras and set fire to three construction vehicles and a resident's car. No injuries were reported.

title: Appeal court upholds life term for killing of Nong Chik SAO official
detail: The Region 9 Appeal Court sentenced a defendant to life in prison for a shooting that killed a Kholo Tanyong SAO official and another person.
note: headline/snippet only

title: Four sentenced to life over 2022 Pattani bombing
detail: Thai Examiner reported four people were sentenced to life imprisonment for a deadly 2022 insurgent bombing in Pattani, with death sentences commuted to life.
note: headline only; court ruling about a 2022 attack; province-level location; coordinates are the provincial capital
